strengths: QuEST addresses a useful computer-vision deployment problem through data-free selective finetuning of temporal and attention-related layers, reportedly updating at most 7% of LDM-4 parameters.

The unconditional-generation improvements are substantial. Table 3 reports W4A4 FID reductions over EfficientDM from 10.60 to 5.64 on Bedrooms and from 14.34 to 11.76 on Churches. Evaluation generally uses 50,000 generated images.

The sensitivity diagnostics and component ablations provide useful empirical motivation. Table 7 improves Bedrooms W4A8 FID from 6.95 to 4.41 to 3.26 as alignment components are added, while reporting 15.25 calibration GPU-hours versus Q-Diffusion's 23.08.

Experiments cover unconditional, class-conditional, and text-to-image generation. The manuscript cites its principal datasets and methodological sources, provides a code link and basic training settings, and acknowledges relevant implications for watermarking and safety checking.
weaknesses: The theoretical contribution is unsound as written. For the stated MSE loss in the output activation, the second-order Taylor expansion is exact regardless of perturbation magnitude, undermining the explanation for PTQ failure in Section 2.3.1. Furthermore, Equation 10's quadratic term in epsilon becomes a quadratic in output residuals in Equation 5 without justification. The argument establishes no sufficiency guarantee for the proposed selective finetuning.

The flagship Stable Diffusion result has limited quality evidence. Table 5 measures only CLIPScore, which does not establish image fidelity or diversity; W4A4 declines from 31.50 to 28.85, and Figure 11 shows conspicuous artifacts across only two prompts. A complementary quality evaluation is needed to characterize the practical usefulness of this operating point.

The ImageNet results require a more careful interpretation. At W4A4, QuEST has worse IS than EfficientDM (202.45 versus 250.90) and slightly worse sFID (7.93 versus 7.75). Simply declaring FID invalid because it improves at lower precision does not resolve the metric disagreement or substantiate broad quality-preservation claims.

The distinctive contribution is primarily the selection and scheduling of finetuned layers, since teacher-supervised finetuning and timestep grouping already have acknowledged precedents. The ablations do not compare progressive versus joint optimization or alternative layer selections under matched budgets, leaving the specific advantage of the proposed strategy insufficiently isolated.

Efficiency comparisons omit the closest finetuning baseline, EfficientDM, and cover only Bedrooms W4A8. No measured low-bit inference latency is provided. Moreover, the disclosed 8-bit attention and boundary-layer exceptions, together with quantization limited to the UNet, require more precise qualification of the 'full W4A4' deployment claim.

Reproduction from the manuscript remains difficult despite the code link: exact selected layers, quantizer initialization and granularity, and conditional calibration and guidance settings are insufficiently specified. These details materially affect both low-bit quality and comparison fairness.
